study type: Case-control study nested within a population-based cohort study
exposure: maternal plasma carotenoid levels (b-carotene, lutein/zeaxanthin, a- and b-cryptoxanthin)
maternal plasma vitamin E levels (a-tocopherol, corrected a-tocopherol, g-tocopherol)
outcome: birthweight <10th centile for gestational age and sex
cohort: The study included pregnant women recruited before 24 weeks of gestation from four hospitals in Montreal, Canada, whose pregnancies were not complicated by pre-eclampsia or preterm delivery, with blood samples taken at 24-26 weeks for SGA cases (n=324) and controls (n=672) with birthweights between the 25th and 75th centiles.
finding: Elevated maternal plasma retinol levels in mid-pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of SGA birth, while elevated carotenoid levels were associated with a reduced risk.
birth_weight: SGA cases: birthweight <10th centile; Controls: birthweights between the 25th and 75th centiles.
gest_age: Exposure measured at 24-26 weeks of gestation; Outcome defined as small-for-gestational-age.
